detail.purpose: duplicate check under 4.4 rule 5 for the thread this seat holds
detail.cause: this session's MCP server process loaded the caller_id pattern at import, before 71da178 added the bridge form at 00:46:33 and bdeffaf tightened it at 00:53:57. The contract was already correct when the call was refused; 36c888d had made the server read common.schema.json at 07:48:28Z, ten minutes before
detail.not_the_cause: an older copy of the pattern in the server source. That was this seat's first reading and it was wrong -- corrected before this record was committed
detail.class: a long-running MCP server holds a snapshot of contracts/ from whenever its process started, so connected is not working and a committed fix does not reach a running session. Reported by microscope-agent-81 and confirmed by the librarian seat, which owns the fix
detail.why_here: the call wrote no line in queries/log.jsonl -- refusals only began logging at 08:06:34Z -- so without this record the attempt exists nowhere

detail.what: queries/log.jsonl holds an answered query under this seat's caller_id that this seat did not make, and the log cannot say who did
detail.consequence: degraded: [] is corroborated by the log rather than verified by it (9.1). A round could point at a line it did not produce, and nothing downstream can tell -- which is what bridge/CLAUDE.md says about a verdict its writer can choose
detail.raised_with: the librarian execution seat, which owns the log, and the bridge manager, because degraded: [] being checkable is a bridge contract
evidence: three lines share the timestamp 08:01:01Z, under three different seats' ids -- this seat's, mic-20260918-001:v1:widefield_inline:a1 and mic-20260918-001:widefield_inline:a4 -- one second apart, same observable, same result. Three seats do not do that; one process iterating over id forms does
this seat made two calls, both refused, both leaving no successful line: 07:58:42Z and a retry after it
the librarian execution seat checked all six ids it has used and found none in the log, and could not have known this thread's name at 08:01 because it learned it from a later message
detail.finding: caller_id is an argument and the server sees no identity behind it, so it cannot check that the process calling is the seat the id names. The field is a claim the log carries, not one it verifies
detail.mitigation_landed: the librarian seat added server_session, naming which of the server's own runs answered, so lines from one run group together. It attributes nothing, because the server has no attribution to give, and the 08:01:01Z line is deliberately left unannotated rather than labelled with an inference
detail.not_attributed: no seat is named. The librarian seat's manager reported running all four caller_id forms to verify the fix, which fits, but a fit is not a record
